long_description:
Overview

Join me on this luxury retreat to reset and re-energise. Workshops, yoga, meditation and plenty of free time with nourishing kai awaits.

You've built a successful life. But somewhere along the way, you lost yourself in it.

You're capable, accomplished, and by most measures, thriving. And yet you're exhausted in a way that a good night's sleep doesn't fix. Rest feels like something you have to earn. Slowing down feels risky. And the idea of a whole weekend just for you might feel almost indulgent. That's exactly why you need this.

A weekend to stop, breathe, and come back to yourself.

Retreat to the stunning Waimea Plains, just 20 minutes from Nelson. This isn't a hustle-harder weekend. It's not a productivity programme with a prettier view. It's two and a half days of genuine restoration, honest conversation, and the kind of clarity that only comes when you finally stop long enough to hear yourself think.

Through facilitated workshops, daily yoga and meditation, nourishing plant-based food, and plenty of unstructured time in one of New Zealand's most beautiful settings, you'll reconnect with who you are beyond what you achieve, and leave with the tools to sustain that beyond the weekend.

Book this unique weekend retreat if:

You've achieved a lot, but you're quietly exhausted and wondering if this is really it
You can't remember the last time you did something just for you, without guilt
Rest feels like something you have to earn, and you haven't quite earned it yet
You're functioning well on the outside but running on empty on the inside
You know the pace is unsustainable but you don't know how to slow down without losing ground
Your identity is so tied to what you do that you're not sure who you are without it
You're successful by every measure, and yet something important feels missing
You need more than a holiday, you need space to think, breathe and reconnect with yourself

What you'll come away with:

A clearer sense of who you are beyond your roles and achievements
Tools to navigate burnout, build resilience, and sustain your energy
A calmer, quieter mind — and practical ways to keep it that way
Permission to rest, and the ability to actually do it without guilt
A personal plan to carry the weekend's insights into your everyday life
Access to my online learning suite to support you across the year ahead

Where and when

Friday 2 April 2027 (from midday) – Sunday 4 April 2027
Appleby House & Rabbit Island Huts, Waimea Plains, 20 minutes from Nelson.

Set on 25 acres of open plains with 360-degree views of the Richmond Ranges, Mt Arthur, and the Waimea Estuary, this is one of those places that slows you down the moment you arrive. Walking and swimming at Rabbit Island, the galleries and cafés of Mapua, and the conveniences of Richmond are all minutes away, but you won't feel the need to rush anywhere.

Accommodation ranges from ensuite luxury rooms to beautiful, private huts with outdoor baths. All rooms have queen beds, a fridge, and tea and coffee making facilities. Shared and private spaces throughout the property give you room to be social or solitary, whichever you need most.

Your package includes:

2 nights' accommodation in your own room
Airport transfers
Facilitated workshops and coaching with Jess
Daily yoga and meditation
Use of the onsite sauna
Healthy, delicious plant-based meals throughout the weekend
Walking and free time to explore the surrounding environment
Goody bag with books and online resources to take home
Access to Jess's online learning suite to sustain you across the year
Massage and additional activities available to pre-book (additional cost)

Accommodation Options

VIP rooms and luxury ensuite huts: $2,495 per person.

Private standard double hut and glamping tent: $1,945 per person. (Three luxury huts all with double beds share two external luxury bathrooms and an outdoor bath.)

20% discount available for early birds using the code EARLYBIRD; limited time only.




Your host: Jess Stuart

I'm an author, keynote speaker, national newspaper columnist, and work-life balance expert with a background in corporate HR spanning 15 years. I've written eight books, including Burnout to Brilliance and Calmony, and I've spent the better part of my career helping high-achieving women build success that's actually sustainable.

I'm also a retreat fanatic. Getting away from daily life has always been where I've had my biggest breakthroughs, which is why, after years of being asked, I finally started running my own. I believe that tapping into your potential doesn't mean doing more or changing who you are. It means uncovering what's already there, and learning to trust it.

I'd love to have you join me.

name: Massey University Food Innovation Youth Summit 2027
venue:
Colombo Hall
Palmerston North, Manawatū-Whanganui Region
long_description:
Overview

Dive into hands-on workshops, tour high-tech labs, and visit actual food factories in the Manawatū .

Food technology combines food science, nutrition, business, engineering and marketing to help shape the foods of the future. Yet many secondary school students have little idea what a food technologist does or how rewarding a career in food technology can be in Aotearoa New Zealand. Our country produces enough food to feed more than 40 million people each year, and our economy is driven by food exports.

Through the Food Innovation Youth Summit, Massey University aims to show Year 12 and 13 students what food technology is all about. Over three days, participants will take part in hands-on activities and workshops designed to bring the subject to life.

The packed programme includes scientific experiments, exploration of emerging technologies and challenges, making food in the Food Pilot (the southern hemisphere’s largest pilot-scale food production facility) and testing their senses in the one-of-a-kind Feast (Food Experience and Sensory Testing) Laboratory. Students will gain a real sense of whether this exciting career path is right for them.

Massey staff from the School of Food Technology and Natural Sciences will be joined by members of the Food HQ regional consortium, including the Bioeconomy Research Institute and local companies within the food valley ecosystem in and around Palmerston North. Together, the team plan to deliver food factory tours that bring laboratory learning to life, alongside authentic university experiences such as staying on campus and connecting with other students from across the country who share a passion for food innovation. Additional activities may include visits to local attractions, creating new flavour combinations using Massey’s soft ice cream machine and enjoying the on-campus recreation centre to round out the schedule.

Students will stay for three days in our Halls of residence on the Manawatu campus (Palmerston North). Meals are provided.

Massey is seeking applications for the 2027 summit. There are limited spaces available. The cost for the course per student a value of $1500, only a $100 contribution required. Bursaries of up to $500 for travel will be allocated to those students that are travelling further to reach the campus in Palmerston North. To apply, students will need to submit a personal statement.




Students need to register by 25th September 2026. Registering via this form is NOT a guarantee of a place in the Summit. A selection process will be undertaken in October and successful attendees will be contacted early Term 4.

long_description:
Overview

A hard-hitting, eye-opening and often hilarious two hour In-person "Parent Cyber Safety Evening"

The "Parent Cyber Safety Evening" covers the following:

Cyberbullying - How bullies can reach our kids 24/7
Social media - How social media is affecting the mental health of 3 out of 5 children. FOMO, depression, anxiety
Gaming and the developing brain – An oversupply of dopamine leading to dopamine deficiency, synaptic pruning, and the underdevelopment of social skills and empathy
Naked Selfies - The pressure to send nudes from intermediate up through high school
Online predators - The methods they use, and how to spot them
Online porn vs healthy sexuality - How consuming online pornography as a child or teen can create a sexual template where violence, aggression, and dominance are seen as normal and consent can become very blurry.
AI - Growing concerns around Companion bots, Deepfakes, Voice Cloning, Algorithmic Radicalisation

Solutions

Filters - Which filters are best and how to install them
Smartphones - How to lock down a smartphone to make it a safe phone
Boundaries - How to put good boundaries in place around device use
3 golden rules - The 3 golden rules that will keep your kids safe
Talking to your kids - How to have difficult conversations with your kids
Challenging our own phone and device usage - Reconnecting as a family.

long_description:
Overview

303 Events and Little Monsters DJs are joining forces for a weekend celebrating the music, friendships and dancefloor culture.

TWO NIGHTS. ONE RAVE FAMILY.

303 Events and Little Monsters DJs are joining forces for a weekend celebrating the music, friendships and dancefloor culture that keep us coming back for more.

🔥 FRIDAY 11 DECEMBER | W.A.M. (WE AIN'T MILLENNIALS)

They said clubbing was a young person's game. Someone forgot to tell the ravers.

Earlier this year, The Listener shone a spotlight on New Zealand's thriving older rave community, the DJs, dancers and lifelong friendships that prove a good night out doesn't come with an expiry date.

Now we're bringing that spirit to Superfina!

Featuring DJs from the article, W.A.M. celebrates the generations who helped build our rave culture and are still very much part of it.

No early bedtime. No slowing down. Just great music, good people and a dancefloor that doesn't care how old you are.

🎂 SATURDAY 12 DECEMBER | LITTLE MONSTERS DJs' 7TH BIRTHDAY

Seven years of monstrous fun!

Little Monsters DJs have spent seven years bringing people together through music, creating welcoming dancefloors and building a community where everyone belongs.

Now it's time to celebrate!

Join the Little Monsters family for a birthday party packed with great tunes, familiar faces and the energy that's kept the party going for seven years.




You don't stop raving because you get older. You get older because time passes. The raving is optional, but highly recommended.

name: Palliative Care for Caregivers starts Thursday 4 March 2027 (for 4 weeks)
long_description:
Overview

This 4 week programme is for Heath Care Assistants, Support Workers, Caregivers working in Aged Care and Community Assisted Living Homes

Palliative Care for Caregivers Programme.

This programme is not suitable for the general public,Nurses, or Allied Health

This workshop is 2 hours per session over 4 weeks and attendees must attend all 4 sessions to gain the Hospice NZ Palliative Care Certificate.
The education is endorsed by Hospice New Zealand and a certificate will be awarded on completion of the programme.

Topics covered include:

Principles of palliative care
Managing physical symptoms
Care in the last days of life
Communication
Understanding loss and grief
Spirituality and self-care

Target audience: Heath care assistants, Support workers and Caregivers working in rest homes & community homes

Max attendees 20: Early registration is advised.

Cost: No charge

Dates: (Attendees must attend all 4 sessions to gain the HNZ certificate)

Week 1: Thursday 4 March 2027

Week 2: Thursday 11 March 2027

Week 3: Thursday 18 March 2027

Week 4: Thursday 25 March 2027

Time: 1000 - 1200 (Attendees are asked to arrive at least 10 to 15 minutes early to sign in).

Limited attendees: Registration is essential

Venue: Nelson Tasman Hospice, 331 Suffolk Road, Stoke, Nelson

Car Parking: We kindly ask if you would please park on Suffolk Road, unless you need to park closer in the car park due to mobility. Please avoid parking near the Hospice’s main entrance on Piwakawaka Road as the road is too narrow for traffic to manoeuvre safely.

name: Massey University Rural Innovation Youth Summit 2027
venue:
Colombo Hall
Palmerston North, Manawatū-Whanganui Region
long_description:
Overview

Dive into hands-on workshops and tour farms and industry in the Manawatū.

Agriculture combines science, technology, environmental management, business, and innovation to produce the food and fibre that sustain people and economies. Yet many secondary school students have little idea what a vast range of careers are available in agriculture or how rewarding it can be in Aotearoa New Zealand. Our country produces enough food to feed more than 40 million people each year, and our economy is strongly supported by agricultural exports.

Through the Rural Innovation Youth Summit, Massey University aims to show Year 12 and 13 students what Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Science and the Environment is all about. Over three days, participants will take part in hands-on activities and workshops designed to bring the subject to life.

The packed programme includes scientific experiments, exploration of emerging technologies and challenges and touring research farms and industry. Students will gain a real sense of whether this exciting career path is right for them.

Massey staff from the School of Agriculture and the Environment will be joined by members of local industry within the rural ecosystem in and around Palmerston North. Together, the team plan to deliver farm tours that bring laboratory learning to life, alongside authentic university experiences such as staying on campus and connecting with other students from across the country who share a passion for all things rural. Additional activities may include visits to local attractions and enjoying the on-campus recreation centre to round out the schedule.

Students will stay for three days in our Halls of residence on the Manawatu campus (Palmerston North). Meals are provided.

Massey is seeking applications for the 2027 summit. There are limited spaces available. The cost for the course per student has a value of $1500, however only a $100 contribution required. Bursaries of up to $500 for travel will be allocated to those students that are travelling further to reach the campus in Palmerston North. To apply, students will need to submit a personal statement.




Please be advised: This summit is NOT intended for students interested in studying Veterinary Science.




Students need to register by 25th September 2026. Registering via this form is NOT a guarantee of a place in the Summit. A selection process will be undertaken in October and successful attendees will be contacted early Term 4.
